q: we were gonna do a couples massage for my birthday and i can’t do it, the sauna and steam room also weren’t recommended, i can’t eat sushi (MY FAV) or cold cuts, and the worst part for me is the lack of energy drinks
cx: Six weeks, just found out; a heavy gym-goer listing what she's been told to stop.

q: i’m getting all the period symptoms that i hate and am so tired ( i literally fell asleep mid meeting, thank god for WFHs) , im like where does it get good 🤣
cx: Same author.

q: The hotel is non refundable, so we won’t get the money back, so I’m wondering if it’s manageable dealing with nausea in your first trimester in a hotel in a different country or whether I should take the money loss and stay home.
cx: UK, five weeks with her first, a 4-day festival abroad booked in two days.

q: I’m also massively worried about the festival itself, which is 4 days, and me dry gagging next to some poor person in the crowd at massive attack.
cx: Same author; she won't be drinking among people she hasn't met.

q: While I was pushing, I heard my mom and the nurse and doctor talking about food trucks and chit chatting.
cx: Looking back at her labour; her mother, now estranged, was in the room.

q: when I put on my playlist that started with a Dixie chicks song my mom was saying she’d listen to Bruce Springsteen and why would I listen to this song now.
cx: Same author.

q: I have had three sweeps now each one week apart. I am convinced they do not work at all.
cx: 40+6 with her second, outside the US; 2cm for weeks with daily contractions.

q: This is my second baby and I am already beyond the time I delivered my first. I am just so tired and I need this to be over.
cx: Same author.

q: And then the tales of motherhood... "you'll never sleep a full night again" "say good bye to all your free time, ever taking a nap again, ever deciding what to again during the evening, say good bye to your personhood its all diapers and Bluey and yogurt drops now"
cx: First trimester, asking whether everyone else is as terrified.

q: What the FUUUUCCKKKKK is there ANYTHING to look forward to this aside from some corny "but youre gonna love your baby SO much more than you ever loved ANYTHING"
cx: Same author.

q: I wish more people shared the positive side and not all the gloom and doom. […] It frightens people who are reading war story after war story!!!
cx: Same author after replies listed good parts.

q: people were not telling me all of this until i got pregnant and we learn a lot through research after we are pregnant. […] Its overwhelming especially when your body is in the throes of nausea and misery.
cx: Same author answering a commenter who knew it all beforehand.

q: My husband's on night shift but our shared hours are in the evening so that will probably be our swing shift
cx: Same author planning newborn nights after a sleep tip.

q: I find it quite minimising when people compare a 20 hour unmediated birth as ‘not that bad’ to a 1 hour ( yep start of contractions - birth of placenta in 1 hour and 11 minutes) birth and how you are lucky for such a quick birth. It is not luck it was brutal and I felt helpless and overwhelmed
cx: UK, about six months after a very fast second birth.

q: My partner wants me to wait until twelve weeks but I feel so miserable not telling them, I hate not venting to my mommy/dad about all the changes I’m going through and having them understand and check on me .
cx: First pregnancy at 9 weeks, scared to tell her parents.

q: Everyone said things get better in the second trimester, but minus a little more energy, I still feel like a hot trash fire.
cx: 16+3, still nauseous most days.

q: some days I feel like I should get a trophy just for showering; it’s such an effort when I feel awful. […] I had no idea how hard this would be. I love this little babe already, but pregnancy isn’t for the weak!
cx: Same author to another commenter.

q: Everyone said to just get thru first trimester and it would get better. And they were right on overall energy, but good lord the gastrointestinal issues. Worth it for the wee one, but holy Moses I was not prepared for the toll it would take. 😬
cx: Same author.

q: I’ve always been warned during my pregnancies about the afterbirth contractions. The ones I experienced after my first two weren’t bad […] But after this last pregnancy, these contractions were absolutely excruciating and unbearable. […] Nobody ever warned me about it being that painful.
cx: Mother of three, a month after the third birth.

q: I have a reminder on my phone set for every two hours to feed him. Do you think it would be alright to change it to like 2 1/2 hours or is he still too young? I’m just really scared he will lose weight or be hungry without me knowing.
cx: First-time mother of an almost four-week-old.

q: I think I have the basics but the lists people share are so overwhelming and seem like too much.
cx: First baby, due next month, asking what was useful and what was a waste.

q: should I take my pump? I know they’ll hospital has them available but I was hoping the lactation consultant could show me how to use mine.
cx: Same author.

q: I warned my obgyn at the start of pregnancy #2 that I was worried I’d panic again, she wasn’t concerned. […] I told them I was panicking and had former birth trauma that was going to make me be on edge. They didn’t believe me.
